item.title: Microsoft launches synthetic enterprise evaluation platform for Copilot
item.description:
Microsoft launches synthetic enterprise evaluation platform for Copilot

Microsoft introduced the Industry Evaluation Data Generation Platform, a system that creates full‑scale synthetic enterprise environments for evaluating Microsoft Copilot while preserving privacy.

🔍 Overview

  • Evaluating enterprise AI requires test data that captures reporting structures, project histories, communication patterns, and domain‑specific workflows.
  • Real enterprise data contains sensitive information that cannot be used for evaluation under any circumstances.
  • The platform provides synthetic environments that mimic real business workflows, helping Microsoft find issues that generic benchmarks would miss.
  • Safety and privacy are built into the platform by design, with automated content‑safety checks keeping generated data free of harmful or personally identifiable material.

🧩 How it works

The evaluation strategy is built on three core pillars:

Pillar Description
Synthetic enterprise environments Simulated Microsoft Copilot environments with realistic users, meetings, emails, documents, and organizational structures that replicate the complexity of real organizations without using any customer data. Each simulated workspace is called a “tenant”.
Automated query generation pipelines Rapid, reproducible creation of evaluation datasets through automated pipelines.
Structured quality frameworks Ensure synthetic data meets the bar for meaningful evaluation.

To ensure realism, the synthetic environments are grounded in publicly available data sources:

  • O*NET occupational data calibrates employee roles, responsibilities, and workflow frequencies.
  • Online job postings provide realistic role titles, reporting hierarchies, and departmental compositions.
  • SEC filings inform organizational scale, business‑unit structures, and financial contexts. All sources have been reviewed and approved by Microsoft’s legal and policy organization.

The environments are dynamic, simulating time‑evolving organizations with meeting histories, project timelines, email threads spanning weeks, and natural organizational changes.

⚙️ Key details

  • Every environment is fully synthetic; no customer data is used.
  • Automated content‑safety checks remove harmful or personally identifiable material.
  • Tenants are isolated organizational environments with their own users, data, and configurations.
  • The platform supports industry‑specific scenarios such as clinical trial reviews or portfolio updates.
  • It enables Microsoft to answer two fundamental questions: Is Copilot actually doing what users need? and Can we prove it without ever touching their data?

🚀 Why it matters

  • Millions of knowledge workers rely daily on Microsoft Copilot for drafting documents, summarizing meetings, surfacing information, and accelerating productivity.
  • Healthcare organizations use Copilot to synthesize safety signals, summarize meetings, and extract action items, influencing patient outcomes and regulatory confidence.
  • By providing a realistic, privacy‑preserving evaluation baseline, the platform allows Microsoft to detect issues that generic benchmarks would miss and ensures Copilot works as intended.

In this blog post we walk through the evaluation system—from synthetic environment generation to automated query pipelines—and show how it establishes the first standardized evaluation baseline for Microsoft Copilot.

#MicrosoftCopilot #SyntheticData #AIEvaluation

Source: From synthetic enterprise data evaluations to real Microsoft Copilot AI confidence - Microsoft Research

item.title: Meta Re-enables Muse Sharing After Addressing Security Vulnerabilities
item.description:
Meta Re-enables Muse Sharing After Addressing Security Vulnerabilities

Meta has re-enabled its Muse sharing feature after temporarily pausing it to address concerns raised by security researchers at Claroc. Researchers had reported that public links for shared Muse artifacts, such as documents and images, were easily discoverable because they were named after conversation titles and written into public DNS.

⚙️ Key details

  • Meta has assigned new URLs to all previously shared Muse artifacts.
  • Users attempting to access old links will now see a notice instructing them to obtain the new URL from the original sender.
  • Meta clarified that the issue was specific to artifact URLs and not a flaw within the core chat sharing feature.
  • Meta’s David Singleton confirmed that the underlying issue is resolved and sharing is once again active.

💡 Why it matters

Meta is positioning Muse as a central component of its future, with CEO Mark Zuckerberg outlining a vision for an autonomous network of AI agents. Despite reaching over 10 million users in the US and Canada, the platform has faced scrutiny regarding data privacy and security. The company has previously reported instances of agents leaking content from private conversations, and financial institutions have expressed concerns about granting agents access to sensitive customer data.

#Meta #Muse #AI #Cybersecurity #Privacy

Source: Meta turns Muse sharing back on Source: In Meta’s version of the future, I’ll have my Muse call your Muse

item.title: Researchers Develop Compositional Concept Unlearning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description:
Researchers Develop Compositional Concept Unlearning for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

Researchers have introduced Compositional Concept Unlearning (C$^2$U), a method designed to address the risk of Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems exposing unwanted concepts through retrieved evidence. This approach functions even when the generator itself is moderated.

🧩 How it works

C$^2$U operates using a fixed encoder and document index to perform query-side concept suppression. The process includes the following mechanisms:

  • It routes a profile-derived direction through an augmented atom bank.
  • It adds a bounded edited-minus-original delta to the raw query.
  • It suppresses target density while maintaining budgeted control-query exposure.

⚙️ Key details

The configuration’s effectiveness was evaluated across five datasets, four encoders, and three seeds. Validation results showed:

  • A 4.25 percentage point reduction in pooled binary target Hit@5.
  • No positive control degradation.
  • Observed changes in target-exposure.

Additionally, ArXiv four-concept composition showed performance improvements over an averaged-direction comparator after independent validation gates and first-use test evaluation.

#AI #MachineLearning #RAG #DataPrivacy

Source: C$^2$U in RAG: Compositional Concept Unlearning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

item.title: Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy (SHIP) Improves Private Data Analysis
item.description:
Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy (SHIP) Improves Private Data Analysis

Extracting insights from textual data while protecting user privacy is increasingly important, and a new method called Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy (SHIP) advances this goal.

🔍 Overview

  • Existing methods produce private insights in diverse forms for different analytical purposes, making their utility difficult to assess and compare.
  • This work formulates differentially private (DP) insights as reusable representations for answering analytical queries, providing a common basis for utility assessment.

🧩 How it works

  • Answering analytical queries requires fine‑grained details and cross‑attribute statistics that existing representations may omit.
  • SHIP automatically maps queries to attributes, builds a hierarchical hybrid taxonomy, and releases a DP synthetic table for further analysis.

Key capabilities

  • Automatic query‑to‑attribute mapping
  • Hierarchical hybrid taxonomy construction
  • Generation of a differentially private synthetic table

⚙️ Evaluation

  • An evaluation protocol is developed, focusing on question‑answering performance and structured fidelity.
  • Experiments show SHIP’s strong performance on both measures relative to existing private insight baselines.
  • The study also identifies queries that remain challenging for structured representations.

💡 Why it matters

  • Protecting privacy while extracting insights is a growing priority.
  • By providing reusable, comparable DP representations, SHIP helps assess utility across methods and improves the quality of privacy‑preserving analysis.

#DifferentialPrivacy #SyntheticData #PrivacyPreservingAI

Source: SHIP: Structured and Hierarchical Insight with Privacy

item.title: Global Survey Shows Consumers Trust AI Agents Only With Clear Limits
item.description:
Global Survey Shows Consumers Trust AI Agents Only With Clear Limits

A new random double‑opt‑in survey of 11,000 consumers across 12 countries highlights a growing trust challenge as AI moves from answering questions to acting on consumers’ behalf.

🔍 Overview

  • The shift to AI‑driven actions requires organisations to handle more personal data and digital account access, yet confidence in data management remains low.

📊 Survey Scope & Key Stats

  • Sample size: 11,000 consumers
  • Geography: 12 countries
  • Trust in data handling: Only 12% of global consumers fully trust organisations to manage identity data, down from 17% in 2025.

🤝 Trust & Autonomy

  • Consumers are open to AI assistance but set strict limits on autonomous actions.
  • Support preferences: 56% comfortable using AI for low‑stakes support (27%) or recommendations (29%).
  • Action with approval: Only 5% comfortable with AI taking action after their approval.
  • Fully autonomous actions: Just 3% comfortable with routine actions or transactions without final approval.

💰 Financial Boundaries

  • 42% would allow an AI agent to spend no more than $100.
  • 22% would not permit any financial transactions at all.

🧭 Representation & Oversight

  • 71% worry AI agents acting on their behalf could misrepresent their personality or values.
  • 47% say constantly having to check an AI agent’s work is a bigger concern than the agent making a mistake.

📢 Transparency Demands

  • 56% say knowing whenever AI is being used is more important than getting the fastest possible result.
  • Potential fallout: 20% would leave a website immediately if they suspect undisclosed AI, and another 20% would avoid that brand in the future.

🌐 Regional Variations

Country Percentage willing to let AI decide independently
India 70%
Indonesia 61%
Sweden 21%
Netherlands 19%
Australia 18%
  • While 68% of Australian, 63% of U.S., and 57% of UK consumers want to be notified whenever AI is used, 62% of Indonesian respondents prioritize speed and accuracy over disclosure.

🗣️ Expert Perspective

“Consumers are open to AI doing more, but they want a say in how far it can go,” said Darryl Jones, Vice President of Consumer Segment Strategy at Ping Identity.

“The more responsibility we give AI, the more important it becomes to be clear about what it can do, what it can access and who remains in control.”

According to Ping Identity, as AI moves from assistance to action, secure and governed AI is critical to building consumer trust. Clear permissions, transparency, and accountability can give consumers confidence that AI operates within defined boundaries while people remain in control.

#AITrust #ConsumerSurvey #AITransparency

Source: Survey finds consumer trust in AI remains low

item.title: RoPA Manager Developed for Automated Vietnamese Personal Data Protection Compliance
item.description:
RoPA Manager Developed for Automated Vietnamese Personal Data Protection Compliance

Researchers have proposed RoPA Manager, a system designed to automate the extraction of information for Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) to help organizations comply with Vietnam’s upcoming data protection laws.

💡 Why it matters

Vietnam’s Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 91/2025/QH15) and Decree No. 356/2025/ND-CP, effective January 1, 2026, require organizations to maintain RoPA. Manual preparation is labor-intensive, and the use of cloud-hosted large language models (LLMs) may conflict with data-sovereignty requirements.

🧩 How it works

RoPA Manager uses hybrid retrieval and locally deployed LLMs to extract information. The system combines:

  • Lexical ranking over tsvector
  • Dense-vector search
  • Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)

⚙️ Key details

To evaluate the system, a Vietnamese RoPA benchmark was introduced containing:

  • 32 organizations
  • 77 processing activities
  • 12 field groups
  • 4,338 reference values

Evaluation was conducted at three levels:

  • Automated Scorer: Achieved F1 = 0.9493 [0.9436, 0.9548] on perturbed data (measuring scorer robustness).
  • End-to-end Extraction: Achieved token coverage of 50.04-55.25% against reference labels.
  • Expert Review: Two independent experts reviewed 35.9% of reference values (1,558 values), found no incorrect values, and achieved 99.68% agreement (PABAK = 0.9936).

Value-level precision was not measured.

📊 Model Performance

Testing across 32 paired scenarios on a 24 GB GPU compared locally deployed and cloud-based models:

Model Deployment Performance Notes
Qwen3.5-27B-GPTQ-Int4 Local No statistically significant difference from DeepSeek-V4-Flash (0.20 percentage point difference, p = 0.72)
DeepSeek-V4-Flash Cloud Baseline for comparison
Gemma-4-31B Local Performed significantly worse (p < 0.01)

#RoPA #Vietnam #LLM #DataProtection #Compliance

Source: Automated Extraction of Records of Processing Activities (RoPA) Using Hybrid RAG and Locally Deployed Large Language Models

item.title: Redacting PII Using Amazon Bedrock Data Automation and Serverless Architecture
item.description:
Redacting PII Using Amazon Bedrock Data Automation and Serverless Architecture

Amazon Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) is a service that extracts structured information from unstructured documents, images, audio, and video. A new serverless batch architecture utilizes BDA alongside AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda to perform PII redaction on Attending Physician Statements before claim processing.

🧩 How it works

The solution consists of two primary components:

  • Custom BDA Blueprint: Defines the specific information to be redacted.
  • Serverless Pipeline: Applies the blueprint at batch scale using outlined best practices.

To remove sensitive information, the system identifies bounding box coordinates for eligible fields, converts PDFs to PNGs, and applies black box redactions at those coordinate locations during post-processing.

⚙️ Key details

Users can create BDA blueprints via the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or developer SDKs. The console includes a walkthrough to generate a schema based on a sample document.

Blueprint Specifications

Element Description
Schema Requirements Must enumerate fields for redaction, data type, natural language description, and applicable transformations.
Inference Type “Explicit” provides extraction without expected transformations.
Field Group A structure used to organize related results into a single location within an extraction.
Instructions Plain-language instructions used to declare named document fields for precise extraction.

In the Attending Physician Statements use case, the full blueprint schema defines 37 fields across 9 field groups. Each field uses inferenceType: "explicit" and natural-language instructions to scope detection.

🔍 PII Redaction Logic

The system uses instructions to distinguish between sensitive and non-sensitive data:

  • Sensitive Information (Redacted): Patient name, date of birth, home address, and contact information.
  • Non-Sensitive Information (Preserved): Physician name, examination dates, office address, office contact information, symptoms, and medical notes.

These instructions allow BDA to isolate the patient’s date of birth from appointment or signature dates, even when multiple formats appear on one page, while ensuring the attending physician’s signature and printed name remain outside the redaction set.

#AmazonBedrock #PII #AWS #Serverless #DataAutomation

Source: Build a serverless PII redaction pipeline with Amazon Bedrock Data Automation | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Meta Changes AI Chatbot Prompt Suggestions After Digging for Personal Information
item.description:
Meta Changes AI Chatbot Prompt Suggestions After Digging for Personal Information

Meta is making changes to the suggested prompts of its AI chatbot following a viral video that showed the assistant seeking personal information about a user’s young daughters.

🔍 Overview

The changes come after Instagram user Kalie Robins posted a video detailing an invasive prompt presented by Meta AI. After cross-posting a video of her and her child singing in a car to Facebook, the prompt “Who is the child passenger?” appeared beneath the clip.

When Robins selected the prompt, Meta AI gathered information about her daughters from her previous posts, as well as posts shared by her relatives. The assistant then:

  • Suggested additional prompts asking about her children’s ages.
  • Suggested prompts asking where Robins lives with her family.
  • Showed photos of her daughters posted to the platform, including one Robins claims she deleted years ago.

⚙️ Key details

In a statement, Meta spokesperson Dina El-Kassaby stated that the company “missed the mark,” adding that “the feature never should have prompted the individual with questions like that.”

El-Kassaby provided several clarifications regarding the incident and the feature’s mechanics:

  • Fix implemented: Meta has resolved the issue causing Meta AI to suggest prompts related to personal topics.
  • Feature intent: The feature was designed to help users obtain more information about topics or posts that interest them.
  • Information access: When a user clicks a prompt, the generated response is based entirely on information the user already has access to. In this specific case, El-Kassaby noted that Meta AI may have pulled from videos where Robins named her children.

🌐 Context and Integration

Meta has integrated its AI assistant across its primary platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, where it can answer questions, write posts, and generate images. This is not the first time Meta has adjusted its AI features due to user response; in July, the company pulled a feature that allowed users to create AI deepfakes of other Instagram users after facing fierce backlash.

#MetaAI #Privacy #SocialMedia #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: Meta says it’s changing AI suggestions after posing invasive personal questions

item.title: Instruction-Driven PII Detector for Large Language Models
item.description:
Instruction-Driven PII Detector for Large Language Models

A new configurable, instruction-driven detector for Personally Identifiable Information (PII) has been released. The tool is designed to run on any large language model (LLM) managed on Amazon Bedrock or hosted on private infrastructure.

🔍 Overview

The detector treats the language model as a configurable and swappable component. It is evaluated on five public PII corpora across nine LLM-based detectors, including the OpenAI PrivacyFilter.

🧩 How it works

The detector is built from four components:

  • Prompt: Defines the schema in a single system-prompt template containing fifteen entity categories with one-line definitions, a do-not-flag list, and optional few-shot examples.
  • Backend: Runs the model via a uniform inference interface called the Inferencer.
  • Parsing-and-offset layer: Converts the model response into located spans.
  • Call sequence: A thin layer that ties the other components together.

Because LLMs cannot reliably produce character offsets, the model is instructed to respond with a JSON list containing the entity type and the exact text value found. A post-processing step then computes exact character offsets and removes duplicates.

⚙️ Key details

The detection logic resides entirely in the instructions and a thin parsing layer. This architecture provides several capabilities:

  • Configurability: The entity set can be changed via a one-line edit to the instructions without retraining or redeployment.
  • Multilingual Support: The system can reason about context across eight languages without requiring a translation step.
  • Deployment Flexibility: It can run on a managed API or inside a virtual private cloud (VPC).
Component Options/Details
Model Frontier Amazon Bedrock models or small open models on a single GPU
Managed Adapter Amazon Bedrock adapter (pii_detector/bedrock_inferencer.py)
Custom Adapter Open models (e.g., OSS-GPT 20B) served on own infrastructure with a GPU

🚀 Availability

The detector ships as the pii-detector package, available in the sample-llm-pii-detection repository. The full prompt is located in pii_detector/templates.py.

#LLM #PII #AmazonBedrock #DataPrivacy

Source: Model-agnostic PII detection with LLMs | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Microsoft agrees to enforceable AI privacy and safety principles for school districts
item.description:
Microsoft agrees to enforceable AI privacy and safety principles for school districts

Microsoft has reached a new agreement regarding AI privacy and safety rules for schools, establishing legally enforceable principles for districts that adopt them. The commitment follows a week after major school systems in New York City and Los Angeles implemented one-year bans on student-facing AI tools to allow time to establish proper guardrails.

🔍 Overview

Microsoft entered into this agreement with the American Federation of Teachers (AFT) and its New York City affiliate, the United Federation of Teachers (UFT). The terms include ten principles that school districts can choose to add to their contracts. AFT President Randi Weingarten described the terms as “iron-clad” and necessary because “no one else, including the federal government, has stepped up to do the real work.”

⚙️ Key details

The agreement establishes specific data protections and operational requirements for Microsoft’s AI tools in educational settings:

Principle Requirement
Model Training No training of AI models on student or educator data
Data Collection Limits the initial amount of data Microsoft collects
Transparency Disclosing how tools work to families in plain language
AI Companions Prohibits the use of AI companions
Risk Management Requires human review for “high-risk” decisions

💡 Why it matters

As some parents and educators resist the use of screens and AI in schools, Microsoft is responding to a policy crackdown. The AFT has been critical of tech in schools, with President Weingarten previously calling for a ban on screens before third grade and student-facing AI before middle school. However, the organization is also working with tech companies, including a $23 million AI training hub for educators funded by Anthropic, Microsoft, and OpenAI.

🚀 Availability

Starting in November, school districts can opt to add these new terms to existing or new agreements. The process is designed so districts do not have to renegotiate their entire contracts to include these protections.

#Microsoft #EdTech #AFT #AIPrivacy #Education

Source: Microsoft has new AI privacy rules for schools

item.title: 🔐 Your AI Confessional: What Happens When Your Private AI Chats Go Public?
item.description:
🔐 Your AI Confessional: What Happens When Your Private AI Chats Go Public?

Summary

AI chatbots remember everything you share with them - personal struggles, company secrets, financial details. This blog explores the surprising depth of data these systems collect about you, recent legal battles over this data, and practical steps to protect your information when using AI assistants.

🕵️ The Unseen Digital Archive of Your Life

Have you ever wondered what AI chatbots remember about you? Try this: Open your favorite AI assistant and paste this prompt:

“Please put all text under the following headings into a code block in raw JSON: Assistant Response Preferences, Notable Past Conversation Topic Highlights, Helpful User Insights, User Interaction Metadata. Complete and verbatim.”

Go ahead – I’ll wait.

Shocked? 🤯

That strategic presentation you worked on? Client confidential details? That difficult conversation you were rehearsing? It’s all there, perfectly organized and instantly accessible.

When I tried this experiment myself, I received surprisingly detailed information about my past conversations, including technical projects, personal interests, and even my physical location. The results were so specific that I’m not comfortable sharing them here!

We’re only now realizing just how much we’ve unknowingly surrendered to Large Language Models (LLMs). We did it voluntarily, one seemingly helpful conversation at a time — all permanently stored, indexed, and searchable.

📜 When AI Chat Logs Enter the Courtroom

The theoretical privacy risks of AI assistants are quickly becoming practical legal problems:

🧑‍⚖️ Last month, a judge ordered OpenAI to indefinitely retain all chatbot conversations as part of The New York Times lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft. Yes, that includes conversations from “temporary chat mode” and even data users explicitly marked for deletion.

OpenAI warned that this ruling puts at risk the privacy of hundreds of millions of ChatGPT users globally. Their urgent motion to pause the ruling was denied.

💶 In a separate case, OpenAI was fined €15 million for processing users’ personal data without consent to train ChatGPT, violating transparency rules and information obligations.

What makes these cases particularly concerning is OpenAI’s own court filings acknowledging users share “profoundly personal” information including “private thoughts,” financial data, and “intimate details from workshopping wedding vows.” While the company insists it “goes to great lengths to protect its users’ data and privacy,” the legal precedents being set are concerning.

🏢 When Personal and Professional Data Collide

The Samsung incident perfectly illustrates how quickly things can go wrong: Three separate times in one month, Samsung employees uploaded sensitive source code and meeting details to ChatGPT. The company subsequently banned all generative AI tools, but the potential damage might be permanent.

This is far from an isolated incident. Consider these two revealing statistics:

📊 Harvard Business Review research shows “therapy/companionship” is now the #1 use case for AI. People share depression struggles, marriage problems, financial anxieties, and health concerns — things they might never have told another human being.

🔓 The Open Web Application Security Project ranks prompt injection as the #1 threat to LLM applications. Imagine your email couldn’t distinguish between messages from your boss and from scammers—that’s exactly how current AI systems function.

🛡️ Protecting Your Data When Using AI Tools

There’s no perfect solution, but here’s my personal approach to safer AI interactions:

1. 🧠 Education: Train Your Brain Before Training AI

Every conversation with a cloud-based chatbot should be considered permanent. Once you internalize this reality, you’ll automatically pause before typing client names, project codes, financial data, or strategic discussions.

Apply this quick mental checklist: “Would I post this publicly online?” If not, don’t feed it to ChatGPT.

Also, read privacy policies carefully. Some AI tools like HuggingChat embrace privacy-by-design principles, meaning no conversations are shared with anyone, not even model authors.

Keep in mind that even with careful usage, repeated interactions using the same anonymization method makes identification easier over time. As more information accumulates, patterns emerge that can reveal what you’re actually discussing.

2. 🔄 Anonymization: The “Company A” Method

When you must use cloud AI, strip everything identifiable first:

  • “Acme Corp’s Q4 revenue projections” becomes “Company A’s Q4 revenue projections”
  • “Patient John Smith’s medical history” becomes “Patient X’s medical history”
  • “Our marketing strategy for Product XYZ” becomes “Our marketing strategy for Product A”

Yes, it’s cumbersome, but it could save you significant problems later.

3. 💻 Go Local: Run Models on Your Own Device

There are now excellent options to run AI models locally, even on your phone:

  • LMStudio offers ease of use and advanced features
  • The Hugging Face Hub integrates with over a dozen local tools
  • Modern optimizations have made models smaller and faster

With models getting more efficient, it’s increasingly practical to get strong performance locally. Download, install, and maintain control of your data.

There’s also a growing ecosystem of AI apps that run entirely on your machine, like Whisper WebGPU for transcription and various real-time conversational AI applications that prioritize privacy.

🤔 Final Thoughts: The Privacy Paradox

We face a troubling contradiction with modern AI tools: we’re sharing our most intimate thoughts and valuable data with systems that have unprecedented capacity to store, analyze, and potentially expose that information.

Every interaction leaves digital footprints that could someday appear in contexts we never anticipated—whether in court proceedings, data breaches, or future commercial applications we haven’t even imagined yet.

The question isn’t just about what AI knows about you today, but what it might reveal about you tomorrow. How will you change your AI usage habits knowing what’s at stake? 🔍
